title: The rundown
note: What's going on right now, in one place. The ↗ links out to the original source; the item's own text turns into a link only once it becomes a full entry here.

items.text: The U.S. economy adds just 29,000 jobs in September and the unemployment rate ticks up to 4.2%, a sharp miss against the 84,000 jobs and 4.1% rate economists had forecast.

Stocks open October on a modest high note: the S&P 500 adds 0.19% to close at 7,666.45 and the Nasdaq edges up 0.04% to 26,871.60, as Treasury yields retreat from their highest levels in more than 20 years.

In the resumed Iran war, Trump says the U.S. will decide "very soon" whether to strike Iran or negotiate, after Iran's response to Washington's seven-day Hormuz proposal arrived through Qatari mediators, even as the 22-day stretch without an Iranian ballistic launch and 26 days without a drone attack mark the quietest intervals since the war resumed.

Brazil votes Sunday, October 4 in the first round of a presidential election pitting Lula da Silva, seeking a fourth term at 81, against Flávio Bolsonaro, son of the former president now serving a 27-year sentence for the January 2023 coup attempt; a runoff follows October 25 if no one clears 50%.

A Gemini 4 Pro checkpoint, unofficially nicknamed "Argon," surfaces on the LMArena leaderboard disguised as "Gemini 3.8 Flash," posting 88% on the DeepSWE v1.1 coding benchmark and 95.3% on Terminal-bench 2.1 — strong numbers Google has not yet confirmed belong to its next flagship model.

"Verity," Amazon MGM's adaptation of Colleen Hoover's novel starring Anne Hathaway, Dakota Johnson and Josh Hartnett and directed by Michael Showalter, opens in U.S. theaters today after a string of release-date delays.
